review_scope: Civil expert evidence under ZPP Articles 243–254, using official PISRS text and its NPB29 working consolidation. Criminal procedure and current professional reporting guidelines are outside this subset.

appointment.summary_en: The court appoints an expert when deciding relevant facts requires specialist knowledge it does not possess.

questions.summary_en: The court identifies the object, puts questions and can require explanations of the findings and opinion.

items_en: Findings (izvid), observations and a reasoned opinion (mnenje).
Written or oral presentation as directed by the court; clarify incomplete or inconsistent findings.

rights_duties.summary_en: The expert must examine carefully and give a conscientious opinion consistent with science and professional practice.

statute.title_en: Civil Procedure Act; official PISRS working consolidation

timestamp.qualified_recognition: Qualified timestamps carry date/time accuracy and data-integrity presumptions; qualification requires the statutory conditions.

open_questions: Provider qualification, certificate status, national filing rules and supported signature formats must be checked separately; this profile does not qualify a TgWitness signature or timestamp.
PISRS labels its consolidated text an informative working aid; verify the applicable amendments and the court order for the case.
No criminal route or standard first-person declaration has been verified here.
The 2020 e-Justice expert factsheet anticipated later reporting guidelines; it is not proof that no current mandatory report structure exists.
Report requirements are summarised in English. Native expert/law terms do not imply a complete reviewed translation of the report or interface.
court_language_notes: Slovenian generally; Italian or Hungarian also have official court use in the respective minority areas. The three languages are not interchangeable in every court.
